userStories.title: Replace sequential dispatch gate with parallel dispatch
userStories.description: As a coordinator, I want the dispatcher to send up to max_concurrent tasks simultaneously instead of blocking on one active task.
acceptanceCriteria: In orchestrator/modules/coordination/dispatcher.py, add count_active_tasks(db, run_id) -> int method that counts tasks in ASSIGNED or RUNNING state
Add dispatch_ready(db, run, agents) -> List[DispatchResult] method that dispatches up to (run.max_concurrent - active_count) ready tasks
dispatch_ready calls DependencyResolver.get_ready_tasks() and iterates results up to available slots
Each task dispatched via existing _dispatch_single logic (agent matching, optimistic claim, board task creation)
If no dispatch slots available, return list with single DispatchResult(dispatched=False, skipped_reason='max_concurrent_reached')
Keep has_active_task() and dispatch_next() as-is for backward compatibility but mark as deprecated
WIRING TEST: Create run with max_concurrent=2 and 2 independent PENDING tasks — both dispatch on same call
WIRING TEST: Create run with max_concurrent=1 and 2 independent tasks — only 1 dispatches (regression)
WIRING TEST: Create run with max_concurrent=3, task_a (no deps) and task_b (depends on task_a) — only task_a dispatches
Typecheck passes
All tests pass
userStories.notes: The dispatcher is at orchestrator/modules/coordination/dispatcher.py. has_active_task() is at line ~78. dispatch_next() is the main method. DependencyResolver.get_ready_tasks() already returns multiple tasks — the current code just takes [0]. For agent matching, each task needs its own agent — prefer different agents for parallel tasks (AgentMatcher already scores availability lower for busy agents). DispatchResult is a frozen dataclass in the same file.

userStories.title: Wire parallel dispatch into coordinator tick loop
userStories.description: As a coordinator, I want the tick loop to execute multiple dispatched tasks concurrently via asyncio.gather.
acceptanceCriteria: In orchestrator/services/coordinator_service.py, update _process_run() to call MissionDispatcher.dispatch_ready() instead of dispatch_next()
Collect all DispatchResult where dispatched=True
Execute dispatched tasks concurrently: await asyncio.gather(*[self._execute_task(db, run, r.task, r.agent_id) for r in results], return_exceptions=True)
Handle exceptions from gather: log errors per task, don't crash the tick
After all executions complete, run reconciler as before
WIRING TEST: Integration test that dispatches 2 tasks and verifies both _execute_task calls happen (mock _execute_task, verify call_count=2)
Existing sequential missions (max_concurrent=1) still work unchanged
Typecheck passes
All tests pass
userStories.notes: coordinator_service.py is large. The _process_run() method is the key one — it currently calls dispatch_next() and if dispatched, calls _execute_task() once. Change to: dispatch_ready() → gather multiple _execute_task calls. Be careful with DB session — each _execute_task should handle its own commits/rollbacks. The reconciler tick runs AFTER all executions complete.

userStories.title: Wire budget admission gate into dispatcher
userStories.description: As a dispatcher, I want to check can_afford() before dispatching each task and pause the mission if budget is exceeded.
acceptanceCriteria: In orchestrator/modules/coordination/dispatcher.py, add _pre_dispatch_budget_check(db, run, task) -> str method returning 'allow', 'defer', or 'block'
Calculate estimated tokens from task.estimated_tokens (set from complexity in US-001)
Compute budget_percentage = (run.tokens_used / run.token_budget_estimate) * 100 if estimate exists
HEALTHY (<50%): return 'allow'
WARNING (50-80%): return 'allow' (dispatch continues, but log warning)
CRITICAL (80-100%): return 'defer' if task_type not in (SYNTHESIS, REVIEW), else 'allow'
EXCEEDED (>100%): return 'block'
In dispatch_ready(), call _pre_dispatch_budget_check before each task dispatch
If 'block': skip task, set run state to PAUSED via transition, emit BUDGET_EXCEEDED event, break dispatch loop
If 'defer': skip this task but continue checking others (synthesis/review may still dispatch)
If run.token_budget_estimate is None or 0: always allow (no budget set = unlimited)
WIRING TEST: Run with token_budget_estimate=1000, tokens_used=950 — heavy task (8000 est) blocked, mission paused
WIRING TEST: Run with token_budget_estimate=10000, tokens_used=8500 — synthesis task allowed, heavy task deferred
WIRING TEST: Run with no token_budget_estimate — all tasks dispatch normally
Typecheck passes
All tests pass
userStories.notes: The existing TokenBudgetManager in orchestrator/modules/orchestrator/stages/token_budget_manager.py has can_afford() but it's complex and not wired. Simpler approach: do the budget check inline in the dispatcher using run.tokens_used and run.token_budget_estimate directly — no need to involve TokenBudgetManager. The graduated response is the key feature. RunState.PAUSED already exists. Use transition_run() for state changes. EventType should have BUDGET_EXCEEDED or RUN_BUDGET_WARNING (check what exists in enums).
